extraction.name: PIQA: Reasoning about Physical Commonsense in Natural Language
extraction.description: A dataset for physical commonsense reasoning, where given a goal and two solutions, models must choose the most appropriate solution.
extraction.creator: Yonatan Bisk, Rowan Zellers, Ronan Le Bras, Jianfeng Gao, Yejin Choi
extraction.publisher: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI)
extraction.citeAs: Bisk, Y., Zellers, R., Le Bras, R., Gao, J., & Choi, Y. (2020). PIQA: Reasoning about Physical Commonsense in Natural Language. In AAAI.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected by asking annotators to provide goal-solution pairs inspired by instructables.com, with a valid solution and a trick (incorrect solution).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Used AFLite algorithm to remove stylistic artifacts and trivial examples; examples with low agreement were removed; data was cleaned of basic artifacts.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were given prompts from instructables.com, asked to articulate a goal and a valid solution, then provide a permutation that makes it invalid (trick). Validation was performed by other annotators; low agreement examples removed.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Examples with low agreement were removed; annotators had to achieve >80% on a qualification HIT; users with low agreement were de-qualified.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Reporting bias: commonsense properties are rarely directly reported; dataset focuses on atypical solutions to avoid prototypical biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Models struggle with physical commonsense; dataset may have artifacts despite cleaning; some correct answers may require expert knowledge.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation for physical commonsense reasoning
